name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.

evidence.explanation: CatalogView.SetCatalogItems concatenates service-returned Picturefilename into the local Catalog image directory at lines 57-58 without filename restriction or canonical containment. CatalogService.CreateCatalogItem (65-70) and UpdateCatalogItem (73-76) persist the supplied model without filename validation. Relative parent-directory segments can select images outside the intended directory under the desktop process identity; attacker needs catalog write access or control of the service response. No arbitrary file-content exfiltration is demonstrated.

name: Relative Path Traversal
description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize sequences such as .. that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

evidence.explanation: CatalogView.SetCatalogItems concatenates service-returned Picturefilename into the local Catalog image directory at lines 57-58 without filename restriction or canonical containment. name: Absolute Path Traversal
description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize absolute path sequences such as /abs/path that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
description: The product allows the upload or transfer of dangerous file types that are automatically processed within its environment.

name: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference
description: The product processes an XML document that can contain XML entities with URIs that resolve to documents outside of the intended sphere of control, causing the product to embed incorrect documents into its output.
